title: Power Automate desktop flows: encrypt and decrypt files with PGP
summary: The roadmap facts, PGP action details, licensing statements and documented control paths are supported. The sensitive-variable logging assurance needs a qualification: a separate Microsoft security notice describes versions where global sensitive variables used in local subflows can appear in execution logs.

claims.claim: Desktop flows have a PGP Cryptography action group for file encryption and decryption using OpenPGP.
claims.quote: The PGP Cryptography group of actions provides a set of tools for encrypting and decrypting files by using the OpenPGP (PGP) standard.

claims.claim: Encrypt file with PGP encrypts a file with the recipient's public key.
claims.quote: By using these actions, you can protect sensitive files by encrypting them with a recipient's public key.

claims.claim: The encryption public key can be supplied as a file path or ASCII-armored text.
claims.quote: Public key source | No | File, Text | File | Whether you provide the public key as a file path or as ASCII-armored text.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Decrypt file with PGP decrypts a PGP-encrypted file with the corresponding private key.
claims.quote: You can also decrypt PGP-encrypted files by using the corresponding private key and passphrase.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The decryption private key can be supplied as a file path or ASCII-armored text.

claims.claim: The decryption passphrase is optional when the private key has no passphrase.
claims.quote: Passphrase | Yes | Direct encrypted input or Text value | | The passphrase protecting the private key. Leave empty if the key has no passphrase.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes these actions as enabling file exchange with external systems and partners that support PGP.
claims.quote: Use these actions to securely exchange files with external systems, business partners, and applications that support PGP encryption.

claims.claim: The encryption algorithm choices are AES-128, AES-192, AES-256, Triple DES and CAST5.
claims.quote: Encryption algorithm | No | AES-128, AES-192, AES-256, Triple DES, CAST5 | AES-256 | The symmetric encryption algorithm to use.

claims.claim: AES-256 is the default encryption algorithm.
claims.quote: Encryption algorithm | No | AES-128, AES-192, AES-256, Triple DES, CAST5 | AES-256

claims.claim: The encrypt action lets the maker choose a compression algorithm.
claims.quote: Compression algorithm | No | None, ZIP, ZLIB, BZIP2 | ZIP | The compression algorithm to apply before encryption.

claims.claim: The encrypt action offers ASCII armor for text-format encrypted output.
claims.quote: Wraps the encrypted output in ASCII armor (text format starting with -----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----).

claims.claim: ASCII armor defaults to off, yielding raw binary output.
claims.quote: ASCII armor | No | Boolean | False | Wraps the encrypted output in ASCII armor (text format starting with -----BEGIN PGP MESSAGE-----). When disabled, the output is raw binary data.

claims.fix: Qualify the logging assurance with: 'Microsoft also documents a sensitive-variable logging issue in Power Automate for desktop versions 2.62 through 2.66 when global sensitive variables are used in local subflows; release 2.67.143.26090 and later includes the fix, and Microsoft lists patched earlier releases.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/power-platform/power-automate/desktop-flows/sensitive-variables-security-update. The cited variables reference additionally qualifies omission from portal Run history with 'if you've logged in with an organization premium account'; preserve that qualification when describing portal Run history.

claims.claim: Desktop flow modules not explicitly placed in a policy group are not blocked even when the default group is Blocked.
claims.quote: Desktop flow modules that aren't explicitly added to any group aren't subject to the default group classification and aren't blocked, even if the default group is set to Blocked.

claims.claim: General desktop-flow data policies classify modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business or Blocked.
claims.quote: Power Automate allows you to create and enforce DLP policies that classify desktop flow modules and individual module actions as Business, Non-business, or Blocked.

claims.claim: The tenant setting is at Power Platform admin center > Settings > Tenant settings > Desktop flow actions in DLP > Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies.
claims.quote:
On the left side panel, select Settings.
On the Tenant settings page, select Desktop flow actions in DLP.
Turn on Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies, and then select Save.

claims.claim: The displayed PowerShell retrieves desktop flow modules, converts them to id/name/type objects and adds all of them to the specified policy's Blocked group.
claims.quote:
$desktopFlowModules = Get-DesktopFlowModules
id=$modules.id
name=$modules.Properties.displayName
type=$modules.type
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -Connectors $desktopFlowModulesToAddToPolicy -PolicyName $dlpPolicy.name -classification Blocked -Verbose
